evidence: The container image the repository builds drops root: its Dockerfile's final USER is a non-root account
expected_output: One observation row per Dockerfile with dockerfile, final_user, nonroot

assertions.description: The final USER directive names a non-root user; a Dockerfile without USER runs as root.

notes: Unevidenced when the repo has no Dockerfile — nothing container-shaped to prove.

plain.checks: Reads the Dockerfile and works out which account the container ends up running as: the last USER line in the final build stage, or root when the file never names one.
plain.violation: The container runs as root. Any code execution inside it starts with full control of the container, and a much shorter path out of it wherever a host mount or a kernel bug is available.
plain.fix: Create an unprivileged account in the image and add a USER line naming it near the end of the Dockerfile, then make sure the paths the process writes to are owned by that account.
